answer: A staking gate works like this: every agent identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if the identity cheats. At the zenith of demand the deposit rises, so spinning up ten thousand fake jade-tagged identities costs ten thousand deposits, while one honest ivory-verified agent pays only once. An attacker therefore faces a real, linear cost per fake identity instead of free copies, and honest agents get their stake back.
